why: All three checks confirm the finding; I could not refute it. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM. curl -sL of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-dependencies.md returns 224 lines; line 11 opens with the claimed sentence character-for-character: 'When you install a plugin that declares dependencies, Claude Code resolves and installs them automatically and lists which dependencies were added at the end of the install output.' The rest of that four-sentence line does NOT reverse it - it reinforces auto-install ('/reload-plugins and the background plugin auto-update reinstall it', 'Re-running claude plugin install ... also resolves any outstanding missing dependencies', 'Dependencies from a marketplace you have not added are left unresolved'). The tag-enumeration half of the claimed behaviour is also verbatim, at :127 ('Claude Code lists the marketplace's tags, filters to those starting with secrets-vault--v, and fetches the highest version satisfying ~2.1.0') and :110 ('Tag each release as {plugin-name}--v{version}') and :45 ('The dependency is fetched at the highest tagged version that satisfies this range'). The page is row 141 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a legitimate Claude contract page, not a Codex/MCP page. (2) CITED FILE. packages/shared/src/plugins/dependencies.ts:15-23 says exactly what was claimed, near-verbatim: 'What is NOT here, and why ... - **Auto-install and tag-based version resolution** (`:11`, `:108`-`:127`). No marketplace source in this repo enumerates `{plugin-name}--v{version}` git tags; every source is a catalog-pinned ref, an npm package or a URL. Resolving `~2.1.0` against "whatever the catalog currently holds" would make a constraint silently mean latest, which is worse than refusing'. The same reason is restated at plugins/types.ts:690-693 and format-adapters/claude.ts:1575-1581. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, one layer up and one down. Down: `grep -a` for `--v` / `git tag` / `ls-remote` / `listTags` across packages/shared/src/plugins/ finds NO tag enumeration anywhere - the only tag-ish hits are npm `dist-tags.latest` handling in install-service.ts:1489-1520 and a GitHub archive-route comment at :1738. Up: format-adapters/claude.ts:1608-1612 pushes a `dependency-auto-install` deferred record whenever a manifest declares dependencies, i.e. the absence is deliberate and surfaced, not an oversight. The disabling consequence is real and live: resolvePluginDependencyErrors (dependencies.ts:68) has two production callers - capabilities/resolver.ts:2150 (via resolveActiveDependencyErrors) and apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:424 - and resolver.ts:1703-1707 sets `enabled = false` with `unavailableReason = 'dependency-unsatisfied'` for EVERY capability of the dependent plugin. So both halves of the claimed our-state hold. SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM TRAP CHECKED AND AVOIDED: install-service.ts has ~40 hits for 'dependenc*', but those are npm RUNTIME dependencies of executable plugins (lockfiles, quotas, `plugin.install.runtime_dependency_*`) - a different subsystem from plugin-to-plugin manifest `dependencies`. The finding names the right one. NOT AN INERT-WORKLIST §3 DECISION: all nine dated owner decisions there were read (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/listSessions) - none is plugin dependency auto-install. NOT A FORK PRODUCT DIFFERENCE either: it is unrelated to the dropped Claude/ChatGPT subscription flows, the corporate gateway, or the NESSY_ rename. CONTEXT THAT DOES NOT REFUTE BUT SHOULD TRAVEL WITH THE ROW: this is a known, tracked, reasoned deferral rather than an unnoticed defect. docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:138 already marks the page 🟨. The parity audit's B1 row (2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:701) explicitly spins it out: 'dependency auto-install becomes its own row (it needs a git-network capability, which is not what "finish B1" means)'. And docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-plugin-dependencies-and-monitors.md §7 calls it 'the one place where the *shape* of what the docs describe is genuinely unbuilt rather than deliberately narrowed', with a hard prerequisite absent from the repo. So the gap is real and open - it just already has an owner-visible record and a home.
correctedState: Confirmed as stated, with two additions. Additions: (a) the absence is actively surfaced, not silent - format-adapters/claude.ts:1608-1612 emits a `dependency-auto-install` deferred record for any manifest that declares dependencies; (b) the disabling consequence is enforced at capabilities/resolver.ts:1703-1707, which sets enabled=false with unavailableReason='dependency-unsatisfied' on EVERY capability of the dependent plugin (not merely a badge), and the same rule is shared with the CLI at apps/cli/src/plugin.ts:424 so `plugin list` and the app cannot disagree. Beyond auto-install, four adjacent doc behaviours are also absent for the same root cause and are recorded in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-30-plugin-dependencies-and-monitors.md §7: range intersection across dependents and its `range-conflict` install failure (:142), the cross-marketplace refusal and `allowCrossMarketplaceDependenciesOn` (:81, :104), `--prune` of orphaned auto-installed dependencies and the provenance bit it needs (:196), and the `no-matching-tag` error (:215). What IS implemented from the page: load-time semver checking via `satisfies` with includePrerelease:false (:48), `dependency-version-unsatisfied` (:214), `range-conflict` for unparseable ranges (:213), fixpoint evaluation so a disabled dependency counts as unsatisfied (:212), transitive enable via resolveTransitiveDependencies and the enabled-dependents disable guard (management-service-v2.ts:694, :741). Status: real, open, already tracked as its own parity row with a git-tag-enumeration prerequisite that does not exist in this repo.
